clauses.text:
Executive Order 10915
AMENDING PRIOR EXECUTIVE OR­
DERS TO PROVIDE FOR THE RE­
SPONSIBILITIES OF THE DIRECTOR  
OF THE FOOD-FOR-PEACE PRO­
GRAM
Whereas American agricultural abun­
dance offers a unique opportunity for  
the United States to promote the in­
terests of peace in a significant way and  
to play an important role in helping to  
provide a more adequate diet for peoples  
around the world; and
Whereas exports of farm products are  
of great importance to the domestic  
economy, furnishing approximately 11 
percent of total farm income; and
Whereas many government functions  
and activities relate to the movement  
overseas of agricultural products and  
commodities, and a number of govern­
ment agencies have responsibilities in  
connection with these activities; and
Whereas it is of fundamental im­
portance that we have a national food  
policy directed toward using our agricul­
tural abundance as a national asset to  
meet foreign policy objectives.
NOW , THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me as President of  
the United States, it is ordered as  
follows;
S e c t i o n 1. Executive Order No. 10900  
of January 5, 1961 (26 F.R. 143), headed  
“Administration of the Agricultural  
Trade Development and Assistance Act  
of 1954, as amended,” is hereby amended  
by renumbering sections 6 and 7 thereof  
as sections 7 and 8, respectively, and by  
inserting after section 5 the following  
new section 6:
“ Se c. 6. Director of the Food-for-Peace  
Program.  Subject to the direction of the  
President, the Director of the Food-for-  
Peace Program (provided for in a letter  
of the President bearing the same date  
as this order) shall be responsible for
the continuous supervision and coordi­
nation of the functions hereinabove dele­
gated or otherwise assigned to officers  
or agencies of the Government. The  
foregoing provisions of this section shall  
not be construed as terminating any  
delegation or other assignment of func­
tion made by other sections of this  
order.”

clauses.label: Sec. 2.
clauses.text:
Sec. 2. Executive Order No. 10893 of 
November 8,1960 (25 F.R. 10731) , headed  
“Administration of mutual security and  
related functions,” is hereby amended  
by adding at the end of Part I thereof a  
new section 111, reading as follows;

clauses.label: Sec. 111.
clauses.text:
Sec. 111. Director of the Food-for-  
Peace Program.  Subject to the direction  
of the President, the Director of the  
Food-for-Peace Program shall be re­
sponsible for the continuous supervision  
and coordination of the functions under  
Section 402 of the Act (22 U.S.C. 1922). 
The foregoing provisions of this section  
shall not be construed as superseding  
any delegation or other assignment of  
function made by the Act or by other  
sections of this order.”

record.reasoning: The structured end dates contradict the claim's own reasoning and the cited sources. EO 12220 (45 FR 44245) section 1-501 revokes EO 10900 as amended and is dated June 27, 1980, but the lead clause's first_end and the whole_order_end say 1977-06-27. EO 10973 section 605(b) supersedes 'Section 2 of Executive Order No. 10915' with section 607 effective as of September 30, 1961, but sec2 and sec111 first_end say 1958-09-30, a date before EO 10915 existed. Identity, inventory (three scopes) and quoted spans otherwise check out, and the EO 11252 later-event treatment is defensible, but a claim with wrong structured end dates cannot be upheld.

versions.research_rationale:
EO 10915 amends EO 10900 (new section 6, Director of the Food-for-Peace Program) and EO 10893 (new section 111); provisional status no. I read the held registered Federal Register text, confirmed identity, and confirmed the dossier’s three-scope inventory (recitals and section 1; section 2; the inserted section 111). Section 2 and section 111 end on 1961-09-30 by EO 10973 section 605 and 607. Section 1 ends on 1980-06-27 by EO 12220 section 1-501, which revokes EO 10900; the 1965 transfer of the Director’s functions (EO 11252) is a later event and an undetermined earlier candidate. The whole-order end is the latest clause end, 1980-06-27.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Searched for ends earlier than the recorded ends. For section 2 and section 111 the first end is the named supersession by EO 10973 (stated effective date 1961-09-30); EO 10924 contains only a negated clause that says it does not supersede EO 10893 and is not an event. For section 1 the dossier lists EO 10972, 11036, 11963, 12148 (amendments of other sections of EO 10900), EO 11252 (transfer of the Director’s functions, a later event that does not name EO 10915 or restate section 6, disclosed as an earlier candidate) and EO 12220 (revocation of EO 10900, the first end). EO 12163 and EO 12220 section 1-502 concern EO 10893 and do not alter the dates above.","independent_command_check":"Each amendatory command was performed on issue; what survived was the inserted text, which ended with its parent order or section. Sections 6 and 111 name the same Director function in two different parent orders and end on different dates; no independent standing command remains.","savings_check":"EO 10973 section 606 is a saving clause for actions taken (accrued effects); EO 12220 has none. See the savings reason.","scope_check":"Inventory of three scopes (recitals and section 1; section 2; section 111) is confirmed from the held text: sections 1 and 2 are amendatory commands and section 111 is the text inserted by section 2. Each scope ends separately; the whole-order end is the latest, 1980-06-27."}

savings_residuals.reason: Section 606 of EO 10973 ("Saving provisions.") continues determinations, regulations, orders and other actions made with respect to any function affected by that order and not revoked or made inapplicable before its date, until amended, modified or terminated by appropriate authority; actions taken under section 111 or section 6 are accrued effects and the functions they concerned were reassigned by EO 10973, EO 11252 and EO 12220. These accrued actions do not keep sections 6 or 111 operative. EO 12220 has no saving clause of its own.
